metadata.title: Fires Secretary of State Rex Tillerson

existing_copy_for_context_only.short: Trump fired Rex Tillerson as Secretary of State and nominated Mike Pompeo to replace him.
existing_copy_for_context_only.medium: On March 13, 2018, President Donald Trump removed Rex Tillerson as Secretary of State and nominated CIA Director Mike Pompeo to replace him. The change shifted the administration’s top diplomatic post from a former oil executive to the head of the intelligence agency. The supplied material records the personnel decision but does not establish a corrupt exchange or obstruction.
existing_copy_for_context_only.long: President Donald Trump announced on March 13, 2018, that Rex Tillerson would leave as Secretary of State and nominated CIA Director Mike Pompeo to succeed him. Tillerson had led the State Department since the start of Trump’s first term; Pompeo’s nomination would move him from the Central Intelligence Agency to the country’s top diplomatic position, subject to Senate confirmation. The supplied record connects the departure to policy clashes and instability in foreign-policy leadership, but does not describe the specific disagreements in detail or establish that Trump removed Tillerson to obstruct an investigation or reward a political ally. The event changed the leadership of the department responsible for U.S. diplomacy and foreign relations. Its consequences for policy would depend on the Senate confirmation and later decisions by Pompeo and the administration.
